title: Books that made me cry (in a good way)
summary: Five books that broke my heart and then quietly put it back together. Keep the tissues close and the tea warm.

books.title: The Book Thief
books.author: Markus Zusak
books.note: Narrated by Death, the story of Liesel, a girl who steals books in Nazi Germany. Devastating and full of love for words.

books.title: Klara and the Sun
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.note: An Artificial Friend watches the world from a shop window, then from the home of a girl who is ill. Soft, strange and heartbreaking.

books.title: A Man Called Ove
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.note: A grumpy widower's carefully ordered life is turned upside down by his new neighbours. You will laugh, and then you will sob.

books.title: Tuesdays with Morrie
books.author: Mitch Albom
books.note: Mitch visits his old professor every Tuesday in the last months of his life, and they talk about what really matters. Short and life-affirming.

books.title: The Remains of the Day
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.note: An English butler looks back on decades of service and the feelings he never let himself say. The quietest heartbreak on this list.
